proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: dimension at a point is invariant under base change (02FY), so one may extend the ground field until two given points are rational, and translation gives an automorphism carrying one to the other, whence equal dimensions; the local formula (02FX) splits dim_g into the local ring dimension plus the transcendence degree of kappa(g); the global dimension is the supremum of local dimensions (02IZ), maximal at closed points where the transcendence degree vanishes (Nullstellensatz, 01T9), giving equidimensionality and the closed-point formula (source lines 1458-1477)

core_obligations: Pointwise equality (proof lines 1459-1465): after extending the ground field (02FY) both points are rational, and translation is an automorphism mapping one to the other, so dim_g = dim_{g'}.
Formula (proof lines 1466-1472): 02FX gives dim_g(G) = dim(O_{G,g}) + trdeg_k(kappa(g)); 02IZ gives dim(G) as the supremum of local dimensions.

Maximality at closed points (proof lines 1472-1477): at a closed point the transcendence degree vanishes (Nullstellensatz, 01T9), so the supremum is attained there and dim(G) = dim(O_{G,g}); with pointwise equality this gives equidimensionality.
proof_roadmap: Show the pointwise dimension is translation-invariant via field extension (proof lines 1459-1465).
Apply the local dimension formula and the supremum characterization (proof lines 1466-1472).
Conclude equidimensionality through the Nullstellensatz at closed points (proof lines 1472-1477).
